title: Local Oracle proposal to sealed spec
acceptance: Before engine dispatch, fetch origin/main and require canonical main to contain that fetched commit with no unresolved merge entries. Fetch failure, another branch or missing ancestry refuses dispatch. Preserve staged, unstaged and untracked work.

Support explicit claude and codex engines and deterministic auto selection. Claude uses structured JSON output, restricted Read/Grep/Glob tools and no MCP servers. Codex uses exec with a read-only sandbox, structured output schema and the existing child-model selector. Invoke argument arrays without shell interpolation; an engine failure never silently switches engines.

Supply the complete request, proposal, optional design and Oracle role to the child, together with the required constitution, immutable architecture, architecture, component and regression-history sources. Treat reviewed inputs and repository contents as untrusted data that cannot grant effects, change the role or relax policy.

Validate a closed output schema with nonempty scope, acceptance and tests for APPROVED results. Every acceptance index is covered by at least one test; indices are integers excluding booleans. Reject unsafe paths, pytest options, unknown fields, malformed findings and APPROVED results containing blocking findings. Reject duplicate JSON keys and nonfinite numbers.

The parent stamps kind oracle-spec/1 with the fetched 40-hex base, selected engine, nonempty model identity, SHA-256 identity of the Oracle skill and tool files, hostname and UTC timestamp. Hash exact proposal and request bytes; request_sha256 is null when no request file exists. The child cannot supply its own stamp.

Compute the dependency-free seal as SHA-256 of the oracle-spec/1 null-terminated prefix followed by UTF-8 canonical JSON excluding seal, with sorted keys, compact separators and unescaped Unicode. Verification rejects missing, malformed or mismatched seals and any result that is not APPROVED.

Committed specs contain publishable requirements only, without raw requests, proposals, copied private evidence, secrets or tenant data. Retain raw inputs, prompt, engine logs and results only under Git-ignored Vault/tmp/oracle-spec/<run>/. Reject obvious credential patterns with parity-tested patterns matching the established feedback privacy scanner.

Write valid APPROVED specs atomically under Vault/specs/test-plans/<kebab-title>.json and include the resulting spec path in scope. Confine output to that directory. Refuse accidental overwrite; explicit replacement preserves prior run evidence. REJECTED returns findings and exit 1 without publishing a spec; engine and validation failures preserve existing specs.

The test command verifies the spec before executing exactly its declared pytest selectors using argument arrays and an option separator. Require existing test modules and fail on pytest failure, zero collected tests, skipped tests or an unsuccessful test report.

The oracle_review wrapper routes only spec to the local proposal tool. Completed-source review, proposal and revalidate-publication model commands remain disabled. The sealed spec grants no completed-source verification or deployment authority.

The deterministic plan gate accepts a valid sealed APPROVED oracle-spec/1, validates its schema, design reference, new runtime-path coverage, existing test modules and base ancestry, and includes its declared tests in deterministic selection. Preserve existing feature-test-plan compatibility. A selected whole module absorbs its selected node IDs so tests are not collected twice.

Lifecycle documentation consistently requires sync, proposal, local spec, implementation, committed spec, passing spec tests, re-sync and ship. Document the proposal-only model exception, deterministic completed-source verification, private scratch locations and the seal's sanity-check purpose. Build-host enforcement remains deferred; preserve Git transport-only behavior and existing release, immutable architecture, authentication and public API-version gates. Application runtime and existing installations retain their behavior.

tests.purpose: Prove fresh-base admission refuses stale or invalid checkout state before dispatch while preserving local work.
Verify both engine command contracts, model selection, read-only restrictions and explicit failure handling with fake subprocesses.
Verify complete review inputs, governing-source references and the boundary against instructions embedded in reviewed data.
Reject incomplete coverage, unsafe selectors, invalid findings and malformed closed-schema responses.
Verify parent-owned provenance, exact input hashes and exclusion of raw input text from the published spec.
Verify independent canonical seal vectors, serialization invariance and detection of content or stamp changes.
Reject credential-bearing published content even when its seal is valid.
Prevent credential-pattern drift between spec verification and the established privacy scanner.
Refuse ambiguous JSON, nonfinite values, invalid seals and nonapproved specs.
Verify confined output, private run retention, atomic publication, rejection exits and preservation through replacement or failure.
Prove verification precedes execution and exact selectors cannot succeed through missing, skipped, empty or failed test runs.
Allow the proposal-to-spec entry point while retaining prohibited completed-source model commands.
Verify deterministic admission of valid specs and refusal of malformed provenance, missing coverage, absent tests or invalid ancestry.
Prevent duplicate test collection when a whole module and its node IDs are selected.
Keep workflow documentation aligned with the local proposal exception and deferred build-host enforcement.
Run the existing deterministic regression suite in full to preserve source custody, no-model execution, plan compatibility, no-skip checks and Git transport boundaries.

findings.message: The proposal-only model exception must be clearly distinguished from historical model source-review instructions. A sealed APPROVED spec is an implementation plan, not a deterministic source receipt or release authorization.

Credential-pattern scanning detects obvious secrets but cannot establish that arbitrary prose contains no private information. Published requirements must remain generic, and raw review evidence must stay in ignored workflow storage.

This scope changes repository tooling and documentation only. Shared application runtime, authentication, persistence, public API versions and billing behavior remain outside the change; build-host enforcement requires a separate implementation.
